clue.text: End of schooldays in America

parts.note: a school term is a stretch of schooldays
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes when school finally finishes for the year in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final stop of a line, the point where it comes to its close.

clue.text: It is found in rediscovered deed and revised

indicators.note: found in says the word It sits inside the scrambled letters
rediscovered suggests the word deed has been turned up in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A document is found again and amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rediscovered' signals the anagram and 'is found in' the container; the surface hides both inside a story about a lost deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been corrected and changed, which is what revised means.

clue.text: Unearthed strong fabric to be taken up

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: denim is a strong cotton twill fabric

explanation.surface: Heavy cloth was dug out and must be lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken up' reverses DENIM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined material has been dug out of the ground, so it has been excavated from the earth.

clue.text: It's a card game, of course

definitions.meaning: a gambling card game in which players stake on cards laid out
a racecourse in Suffolk, the home of British horse racing

explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk town is famous for its racecourse, the headquarters of British flat racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a betting card game and to the famous English racecourse.

clue.text: Determined to attack

definitions.meaning: set on, resolved to do something
to fall upon or assault someone

explanation.definitionFit: Being resolved on something is one sense of the phrase; assaulting someone is the other.

clue.text: Physical exercises I put off when on board

indicators.note: being on board places the scrambled letters inside the ship's two letters

parts.note: on board a ship means aboard the SS, the abbreviation for a steamship

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of I put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger admits skipping the workout while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram; 'on board' means inside SS, the crossword's standard steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are a familiar abdominal workout, so they count as physical exercises.

clue.text: Firm one's engaged by was traded

indicators.note: being engaged by is being held within, so the I goes inside the other word

parts.note: sold means was traded
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A company's one is involved in what was sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is firm, hard and unyielding to the touch.

clue.text: Try out striker in international game

parts.note: to test is to try out
a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A selector trials a centre forward in a game for the national team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer but is a match. A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a top-level game between national sides, chiefly in cricket.

clue.text: With great insight, golf club has filled coaching vacancy

definitions.text: golf club has filled coaching vacancy
definitions.meaning: read as two words: a professional coach has been located

explanation.surface: A golf club wisely appoints a new coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means deeply insightful; split, it says a club pro has been obtained.

clue.text: Examine success right away

parts.note: a win is a success
now means immediately, right away

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrutinise a triumph without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow is to sift through something carefully, separating good from bad, as in examining evidence.

clue.text: Discuss business in express store

parts.note: to express something is to talk, put it into words
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Staff chat about work in a convenience store that sells fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like an adjective for a fast shop; it is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to talk shop means to discuss one's work or trade, especially socially.

clue.text: A leading light in the motorist's world

definitions.text: A leading light in the motorist's world

parts.words: A leading light in the motorist's world
parts.note: a leading light is usually a prominent person; here it is literally the lamp at the front of a car

explanation.surface: Praise for a top figure among drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front lamp literally leads the vehicle and lights the road ahead, a pun on the idiom.

clue.text: Mother and child in a jam?

parts.note: a dam is a mother, chiefly of animals
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A parent and child find themselves in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jam' reads as trouble; the question mark flags that the fruit preserve is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Damson is a small plum commonly made into jam, so the word can name that preserve by example.

clue.text: Being opposed to the building of seats for spectators?

definitions.meaning: resisting firmly, taking a position against something

definitions.text: the building of seats for spectators?

explanation.definitionFit: Holding firm against something is an idiom for resistance; read literally it is erecting a grandstand.

clue.text: Improvised fashion garment

parts.note: to fashion is to make
a shift is a simple dress

explanation.surface: A fashion item thrown together quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun about clothes but is the verb meaning make.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a temporary substitute put together from what is available.

clue.text: Unexpectedly entering with a South American

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Someone from South America walks in by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges ENTERING plus A; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argentine is a person from Argentina, a country of South America.

clue.text: Laird can set out to be chief

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner is able to set off as leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges LAIRD CAN. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means principal or of chief importance, as in cardinal sin.

clue.text: What one is encouraged to do on a psychiatrist's couch

definitions.text: What one is encouraged to do on a psychiatrist's couch

parts.words: What one is encouraged to do on a psychiatrist's couch
parts.note: a patient in therapy is invited to speak freely and at length

explanation.surface: A description of the therapy patient's role.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking extensively is exactly what a therapist hopes a reclining patient will do.

clue.text: Hole in ten unusually high

indicators.note: in places the hole inside the scrambled letters
unusually suggests the letters of ten appear in an unusual order

parts.note: a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A golfer gets a hole in one at an unusually lofty course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals the anagram and 'in' the container; 'Hole in' tempts a golfing reading, but the hole is a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone of high rank or distinction.

clue.text: An old one will be experienced — in the theatre?

definitions.text: An old one will be experienced — in the theatre?

parts.words: An old one will be experienced — in the theatre?
parts.note: a veteran; the question mark invites a whimsical reading as one who works on stage

explanation.surface: A veteran actor knows the ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom old stager means a seasoned veteran, and playfully suggests a performer long on the boards.

clue.text: Inventor having no team for back-up?

indicators.note: back-up in a down-to-up sense: the letters of no and team are read from the end backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An inventor with no squad to support him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for back-up' reads as support, but signals reading NO SIDE in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Loop-line soon turns east

indicators.note: turns says the word soon is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway branch line will shortly head eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'east' as the definition and hid the answer in 'line soon'; but a noose is a loop of line, so 'Loop-line' defines it and 'east' supplies the final E after SOON reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop formed in a rope or cord, a loop of line.

clue.text: Modernise old pub at first — tea breaks after five

indicators.note: says the pub comes first, ahead of the old
after says the broken tea follows the five

parts.note: an inn is a pub
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of tea are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord updates an old pub, with a cuppa breaking up the afternoon after five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' is the anagram signal, 'after' orders the last piece, and 'at first' says the pub precedes the old in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new methods, which is what modernising something involves.

clue.text: It's still produced in Russia

parts.note: still looks like an adverb meaning yet, but is a distilling apparatus

explanation.surface: Something continues to be made in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is the spirit distilled in a still and famously made in Russia.

clue.text: Poison counter

parts.note: something that counters a poison, though it reads like someone counting poisons

explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that neutralises a toxin is exactly what works against a poison.

clue.text: Looking blue, I'd go in for treatment

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A depressed patient says they would go to hospital to be treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' rearranges the letters of I'D GO IN; 'Looking' is a link, and 'blue' feigns sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade between violet and the blue of the spectrum.

clue.text: Unwilling to be clad in Anglican dress

indicators.note: being clad in means being enclosed, so the unwilling word goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
loth means reluctant, unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to wear vestments of the English church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be clad in' signals the container. The Church of England is Britain's established Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to dress them, putting garments on them.

clue.text: Hear suit about writers' needs when lacking an alternative

definitions.text: writers' needs when lacking an alternative

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd scene of a lawsuit being heard, writers short of a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges HEAR SUIT; the long definition describes a word book consulted when a writer cannot find another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri list synonyms, the reference books writers reach for when stuck for a different word.
